what: How each Florida place voted in five contests of the 2020, 2022 and 2024 general elections: the votes for the Democratic candidate or ticket, the Republican candidate or ticket, every other candidate printed on the ballot together, and the total of those. Counties' figures are the Florida Department of State's certified county results; state House and Senate districts are added up from the official returns each county's supervisor of elections submitted to the Division of Elections, precinct by precinct.
note: What this is: how the people of a place voted in that election, from the official results: the certified county figures, added up by county, school district (each Florida county is one), judicial circuit and district court of appeal's district (whole counties), and, for 2022 and 2024, each precinct's official returns added up by state House and Senate district on the plans still in force for 2026, only where every precinct can be placed in one district without estimating. Write-ins are left out: Florida counts a write-in only for a qualified write-in candidate, and those few votes cannot be placed by precinct. What this is not: it is not a prediction of any election; it says nothing about any candidate on a later ballot or about any voter; a nonpartisan office stays nonpartisan; and a district's figures are for its lines of that year. The candidates and tickets are named only to say which election this was. In a place with very few voters the split would come close to saying how particular people voted, so there the split is left out.

few.why: A place's too_few lists the contests in which it had fewer than 20 votes, or in which every vote went the same way. There the split comes close to saying how particular people voted, so a page should leave it out. The counts are kept here all the same, so that the sums can be checked.

not_given: Cities and towns are not added up: no Florida city or town is among our places, and the precinct results do not say which city a precinct lies in. County commission districts are not added up: the precinct results show a precinct's commission district only where that district's seat was on that year's ballot, many counties elect every commissioner countywide, and no statewide list a script can read says which district each precinct lies in. Hospital, fire and other special districts are not added up, and neither are congressional districts (the 2026 plan was not in force at these elections).

judicial.what: Judicial circuits and district courts of appeal's districts, as whole counties

house.what: State House districts (H000H8013), enacted 2022, the plan in force for 2022, 2024 and 2026
house.why_not: A district is missing in a year when a precinct that may lie in it could not be placed in one district alone (Florida precincts are often split between districts, and their results are given whole), or when a county it reaches has precinct results that do not add up to its certified figures: nothing is divided by estimate here. The 2020 election was held on the districts of the 2010s; the plans enacted in 2022 were first used that year, so 2020 is not given.
house.note: A district is its precincts added up, each precinct placed by the contests it voted in, the Legislature's plan (which districts reach its county) and the same precinct in the other election on the same lines.
